title: GitHub - brookstalley/hallucinote: Hallucinote — DB-backed authoring for Ableton Live
excerpt: Hallucinote — DB-backed authoring for Ableton Live - brookstalley/hallucinote
content_html:
Describe what you're after, hear it, argue with it — music as code you can read, fork and rewrite.

Say what you're going for, and it gets built into a running Live set — build.py for the notes, a snapshot for the instruments and mix. Then listen, change your mind, explore new ideas. Because the song is code in a git directory, trying the half-time bridge or a key change costs a branch and a minute: keep it, or throw it away and try the next one.

Round-trip to Ableton, recording MIDI events in Ableton to pull back and work on in Hallucinote (no audio round trip... yet).

See it

Accelerated video: from prompt to finished arrangement.

demo-video-README.mp4

The chat is staged so the build runs under the conversation and there is something to watch; real sessions are more iterative and take longer.

A different song, made the same way, ships in this repo as source:

"Make a 2-minute punk song that crams the chord progression of Beethoven's 5th into those two minutes. Drums, bass, rhythm guitar, and vocals emulated by a lead guitar. Call it punk-fate."

This prompt is cheating a bit, because it implicitly specifies arrangement and harmony. But it allowed a ~45 minute build, iterating on micro timing (punk's not dead!), instrumentation, and mixing and production. It took a couple of sessions to get right, always with the user in charge. The result:

▶ Listen — punk-fate, 1:58 · The finished song ships here as source: examples/punk-fate/.

Getting there runs fourteen ordered phases:

tempo → meter → tracks → returns → scenes → clips →
mix → devices → routing → device-sidechain → envelopes →
performed automation → arrangement → cues

Want the bridge to hit harder? "Lift the lead an octave in the bridge, and make the chorus drums drag." Claude edits the code and re-pushes, changing what you asked for and leaving the rest alone.

Beat by beat, with the transcript, the screenshots and the mix numbers: the tour.

How it works

  • You decide; it writes the decision down. Notes, arrangement and automation in build.py; instruments, chains and the dialed mix in a snapshot. Every choice is legible afterwards — you can read what was done, and why, and change it.
  • The notes come from generators you can read. Parametric Python — tresillo, walking_bass, kit abstractions, per-part feel. Claude's craft is choosing which to call and with what musical parameters, then writing that down. What lands in Live is MIDI and mixer state in a session you own outright.
  • Push materializes; pull ingests. Push drives the song into a fresh or existing set; pull folds your manual Live edits back in. Re-runs are idempotent.
  • It listens back, and tells you straight. Ask "is the chorus landing?" and Claude reads the composition, or renders the set and measures masking, loudness and groove, against the intent you declared — then reports what it found and what it would change. Real numbers, and an opinion you can overrule.

Who it's for

  • Curious how songs get put together. Ask for something, then ask why it works that way. It proposes with the reasoning showing — "E minor, so the chorus can lift into the relative major" — and you can overrule it and hear the difference straight away. You learn the craft by watching choices get made, then making better ones.
  • Playing already, and reaching further. The arrangement you can hear in your head but would spend a week programming: a bassline weaving between two different kick patterns, thirty-two bars of hats that breathe, a polyrhythmic bridge. Ask for it and listen to it.
  • Deep in it. Leverage. Bulk edits you'd otherwise script by hand, chorus variants on branches you A/B and discard, and a review pass that measures masking, loudness and timing against the intent you declared — then tells you where it disagrees. A second opinion with numbers behind it is rarer than it should be.

What to ask for

  • Any genre, any shape. Conceptual ("a song about overcoming loss"), musical ("a Baroque prelude in G minor from a single broken-chord figuration"), or stylistic ("Duran Duran if they dropped acid with Black Sabbath").
  • Under-specify on purpose. Claude works out what your prompt leans on (/hallucinote:song-brief) — key, tempo, what a named turn means musically — and comes back once with proposals you can wave through or redirect in a word.
  • Share and fork. A collaborator clones the directory; Hallucinote checks their plugins first and names anything missing.

Status

Actively developed, and honest about the rough edges:

  • Platforms: Ableton Live 12 on macOS and Windows (Ableton ships no Linux build). macOS is where it's developed day to day; the Windows paths are implemented and unit-tested, with fewer real sessions behind them.
  • Editions: the full authoring loop is exercised on Live 12 Standard and Suite. Only the measured mix review needs Max for Live (Suite, or the add-on for Standard); without it, review is symbolic: it reads the score. Intro and Lite are untested, and their track limits will bite.
  • The melody is yours. Sketch a topline in Live and it arranges, sound-designs and mixes the whole track underneath, then reads the line back against your intent — contour, intervals, how it sits on the chords. How that works. Sung vocals are on the list; today the synth sings.
  • Boundaries: MIDI and the mix are what it builds; a recorded vocal take can't yet be read back through the bridge.
  • What it costs to run: Hallucinote is free; the Claude usage behind it bills to your plan. A song is a long agentic session — the worked example above ran about forty minutes of continuous agent work, and each measured mix pass hands back a sizeable analysis payload. Expect a full compose-and-mix session to eat a real share of a Claude plan's budget. /cost reports what a session actually used. Live 12 (and Max for Live for the measured review) is the other bill.

The rest, each with its workaround: Known issues.

Install

The plugin is self-contained — skills, Ableton bridge and composing engine in one managed environment. Nothing else to clone or track.

1. Prerequisites — Claude Code, Ableton Live 12, and uv (brew install uv on macOS, winget install astral-sh.uv on Windows). uv provisions the Python the plugin needs, so you don't install one.

2. Install the plugin — in Claude Code:

/plugin marketplace add brookstalley/hallucinote
/plugin install hallucinote@hallucinote

3. Connect Ableton — quit Live, run /hallucinote:ableton-mcp-install (it installs the Remote Script and analyzer, the one thing the plugin can't do for you). Reopen Live and assign Hallucinote to a free Control Surface slot in Preferences → Link, Tempo & MIDI. Restart Claude Code.

4. Verify — ask Claude "get the current set's info from Ableton." Tempo, signature and track counts coming back means the bridge works.

Hacking on the framework itself? Load it from your checkout with claude --plugin-dir /path/to/hallucinote — see CONTRIBUTING.md.

Your first song

Open Live with an empty set, start Claude Code wherever your songs live (any folder — Claude offers to create the workspace), and describe a song. Unsure about your setup? Run /hallucinote:getting-started first.

The Quickstart walks the first song end to end in ten minutes.

Troubleshooting

  • "Version mismatch" / "handshake missing" — bridge and Remote Script have diverged, usually after an update. Rerun /hallucinote:ableton-mcp-install, then fully quit and reopen Live (it caches Control Surface modules at startup).
  • Session info hangs or "no connection" — Live isn't running, the Control Surface slot isn't assigned, or Claude Code wasn't restarted after assigning it.
  • Anything else — ask Claude to run preflight; it reports what the installer can and can't find. More in the FAQ.

Bugs go to issues; report vulnerabilities privately instead — see SECURITY.md.

Learn more

If you want to… Read
See everything you can ask for docs/skills.md
Understand the whole song-making lifecycle docs/song-workflow.md
Share a song with a collaborator docs/collaboration.md
Understand the design philosophy docs/VISION.md
Read or edit a song's build.py docs/song-authoring-conventions.md
See what changed in a release CHANGELOG.md
Contribute code CONTRIBUTING.md
Browse all the docs docs/README.md

Project layout

src/hallucinote/      # composition engine: db, generators, sync, capture
hallucinote_mcp/      # the MCP bridge server (13 unified Ableton tools)
skills/               # the /hallucinote:* Claude Code skills the plugin ships
docs/                 # quickstart, tour, conventions, FAQ, schemas, …

This is the framework. Your songs live in their own repo, one directory each: build code, mix snapshot, decisions, tests.

License

MIT. See LICENSE.

sentences.zh: 它提出的推理显示——“E小调，这样副歌可以升到相对大调”——你可以否决它并立即听到区别。

sentences.en: You learn the craft by watching choices get made, then making better ones.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过观察做出的选择来学习技巧，然后做出更好的选择。

blocks.html_en: • Playing already, and reaching further. The arrangement you can hear in your head but would spend a week programming: a bassline weaving between two different kick patterns, thirty-two bars of hats that breathe, a polyrhythmic bridge. Ask for it and listen to it.

sentences.en: Playing already, and reaching further.
sentences.zh: 已经在玩了，而且还更进一步。

sentences.en: The arrangement you can hear in your head but would spend a week programming: a bassline weaving between two different kick patterns, thirty-two bars of hats that breathe, a polyrhythmic bridge.
sentences.zh: 这种编曲你可以在脑海中听到，但需要花一周的时间来编程：在两种不同的底鼓模式之间编织的低音线、三十二个会呼吸的小节、一个多节奏的桥梁。

sentences.en: Ask for it and listen to it.
sentences.zh: 求之并听之。

blocks.html_en: • Deep in it. Leverage. Bulk edits you'd otherwise script by hand, chorus variants on branches you A/B and discard, and a review pass that measures masking, loudness and timing against the intent you declared — then tells you where it disagrees. A second opinion with numbers behind it is rarer than it should be.

sentences.en: Deep in it.

sentences.en: Leverage.

sentences.en: Bulk edits you'd otherwise script by hand, chorus variants on branches you A/B and discard, and a review pass that measures masking, loudness and timing against the intent you declared — then tells you where it disagrees.
sentences.zh: 批量编辑您原本需要手动编写的脚本，您 A/B 并丢弃的分支上的合唱变体，以及根据您声明的意图测量掩蔽、响度和时间的审查通道 - 然后告诉您它不同意的地方。

sentences.en: A second opinion with numbers behind it is rarer than it should be.
sentences.zh: 有数字支持的第二种意见比应有的情况要少见。

content_html_zh:
描述你所追求的东西，聆听它，与之争论——音乐就是你可以阅读、分叉和重写的代码。

说出你想要什么，它就会内置到正在运行的现场设置中 - build.py 用于音符，用于乐器和混音的快照。 然后倾听，改变想法，探索新想法。 因为这首歌是 git 目录中的代码，所以尝试中场桥接或调性更改会花费一个分支和一分钟：保留它，或者扔掉它并尝试下一个。

往返 Ableton，在 Ableton 中记录 MIDI 事件，然后在 Hallucinote 中进行处理（无音频往返... 然而）。

See it

加速视频：从提示到完成排列。

demo-video-README.mp4

聊天是分阶段进行的，因此构建在对话下运行，并且有一些东西值得关注；真正的会话更加迭代并且需要更长的时间。

以相同方式制作的另一首歌曲作为源在此存储库中提供：

“制作一首 2 分钟的朋克歌曲，将贝多芬第五交响曲的和弦进行塞进这两分钟。 鼓、贝斯、节奏吉他和主音吉他模拟的人声。 称之为朋克命运。”

这个提示有点作弊，因为它隐含地指定了排列和和声。 但它允许大约 45 分钟的构建、迭代微计时（朋克还没有死！）、乐器、混音和制作。 需要几次会话才能完成任务，并且始终由用户负责。 结果：

▶ 听 — punk-fate，1:58 · 完成的歌曲作为来源发送至此处：examples/punk-fate/。

到达那里需要经历十四个有序的阶段：

tempo → meter → tracks → returns → scenes → clips →
mix → devices → routing → device-sidechain → envelopes →
performed automation → arrangement → cues

想要桥梁受到更大的冲击吗？ “将琴桥上的主音提升一个八度，让合唱团的鼓声拖曳。” 克劳德编辑代码并重新推送，更改您要求的内容并保留其余部分。

一个接一个的节拍、文字记录、屏幕截图和混音号码：巡演。

它是如何运作的

  • 你决定；它把决定写下来。 build.py 中的注释、排列和自动化；快照中的乐器、链条和拨出的混音。 每个选择之后都清晰可见——您可以阅读所做的事情、原因，并进行更改。
  • 这些注释来自您可以阅读的生成器。 参数化 Python — tresillo、walking_bass、套件抽象、每个部分的感觉。 克劳德的技巧是选择调用哪个以及使用什么音乐参数，然后将其写下来。 Live 中的内容是您完全拥有的会话中的 MIDI 和混音器状态。
  • 推动实现；拉摄取。 Push 将歌曲驱动到新的或现有的集合中；拉回折叠您的手动实时编辑。 重新运行是幂等的。
  • 它会倾听，并直接告诉你。 问“合唱团落地了吗？” 克劳德（Claude）阅读构图，或渲染设置并根据您声明的意图测量掩蔽、响度和律动 - 然后报告它发现了什么以及它将改变什么。 真实的数字，以及你可以否决的观点。

这是给谁的

  • 很好奇歌曲是如何组合在一起的。 要求一些东西，然后问为什么会这样。 它提出的推理显示——“E小调，这样副歌可以升到相对大调”——你可以否决它并立即听到区别。 你可以通过观察做出的选择来学习技巧，然后做出更好的选择。
  • 已经在玩了，而且还更进一步。 这种编曲你可以在脑海中听到，但需要花一周的时间来编程：在两种不同的底鼓模式之间编织的低音线、三十二个会呼吸的小节、一个多节奏的桥梁。 求之并听之。
  • 深陷其中。 杠杆作用。 批量编辑您原本需要手动编写的脚本，您 A/B 并丢弃的分支上的合唱变体，以及根据您声明的意图测量掩蔽、响度和时间的审查通道 - 然后告诉您它不同意的地方。 有数字支持的第二种意见比应有的情况要少见。

需要什么要求

  • 任何流派，任何形状。 概念性的（“一首关于克服失落的歌曲”）、音乐性的（“由一个断弦形象组成的G小调巴洛克前奏曲”）或风格性的（“如果他们在《黑色安息日》中掉下酸液，杜兰·杜兰”）。
  • 故意指定不足。 克劳德弄清楚你的提示所依赖的内容（/hallucinote:song-brief）——调、节奏、命名的转弯在音乐上的含义——然后回来一次，提出你可以挥手或用一句话重定向的建议。
  • 分享和分叉。 协作者克隆该目录； Hallucinote 首先检查他们的插件并指出缺少的任何内容。

地位

积极开发，并对粗糙边缘诚实：

  • 平台：macOS 和 Windows 上的 Ableton Live 12（Ableton 不提供 Linux 版本）。 macOS 是它日常开发的地方； Windows 路径已实现并经过单元测试，其背后的实际会话较少。
  • 版本：完整的创作循环在 Live 12 Standard 和 Suite 上进行。 只有测量的混音审核需要 Max for Live（Suite，或 Standard 的附加组件）；没有它，复习只是象征性的：它读取分数。 Intro 和 Lite 未经测试，它们的曲目限制将会受到影响。
  • 旋律是你的。 在 Live 中绘制一条顶线，它会对下面的整个曲目进行编排、声音设计和混合，然后根据您的意图读回这条线——轮廓、音程、它在和弦上的位置。 这是如何运作的。 演唱者的声音也在名单上；今天合成器唱歌了。
  • 边界：MIDI 和混音是它所构建的；录制的声音还无法通过桥读回。
  • 运行成本：Hallucinote 是免费的；其背后的克劳德使用量将按您的计划计费。 一首歌是一个漫长的代理会话——上面的工作示例运行了大约四十分钟的连续代理工作，并且每个测量的混音传递回了相当大的分析有效负载。 预计完整的作曲和混音会议将占用克劳德计划预算的真正份额。 /cost 报告会话实际使用的内容。 Live 12（以及用于衡量评论的 Max for Live）是另一项法案。

其余的都有其解决方法：已知问题。

安装

该插件是独立的 - 技能、Ableton Bridge 和作曲引擎位于一个托管环境中。 没有其他可克隆或跟踪的内容。

1. 先决条件 — Claude Code、Ableton Live 12 和 uv（在 macOS 上brew install uv，在 Windows 上 winget install astral-sh.uv）。 uv 提供了插件所需的 Python，因此您无需安装。

2. 安装插件 - 在 Claude 代码中：

/plugin marketplace add brookstalley/hallucinote
/plugin install hallucinote@hallucinote

3. 连接 Ableton — 退出 Live，运行 /hallucinote:ableton-mcp-install （它会安装远程脚本和分析器，这是该插件无法为您做的一件事）。 重新打开 Live 并将 Hallucinote 分配到首选项 → 链接、速度和 MIDI 中的空闲控制界面插槽。 重新启动克劳德代码。

4. 验证 — 询问 Claude“从 Ableton 获取当前集合的信息。” 速度、签名和曲目计数的返回意味着桥梁可以正常工作。

攻击框架本身？ 使用 claude --plugin-dir /path/to/hallucinote 从结账处加载它 — 请参阅 CONTRIBUTING.md。

你的第一首歌

使用空集打开 Live，在您的歌曲所在的任何位置（任何文件夹 - Claude 提供创建工作区）启动 Claude Code，并描述歌曲。 不确定您的设置？ 首先运行 /hallucinote:getting-started。

快速入门将在十分钟内将第一首歌曲从头到尾播放完。

故障排除

  • “版本不匹配”/“握手缺失”——桥和远程脚本出现分歧，通常是在更新后。 重新运行 /hallucinote:ableton-mcp-install，然后完全退出并重新打开 Live（它在启动时缓存控制界面模块）。
  • 会话信息挂起或“无连接” - Live 未运行，未分配控制界面插槽，或者 Claude Code 在分配后未重新启动。
  • 任何其他事情 - 让克劳德进行预检；它报告安装程序可以找到什么和找不到什么。 更多信息请参见常见问题解答。

Bug 会导致问题；相反，请私下报告漏洞 - 请参阅 SECURITY.md。
